analysis.alignment_check: Both mask variants use lea -1(page_size), test addr,mask, conditional branch; no integer divide executes in the address-validation/lookup portion of a normal resident hit.
analysis.remaining_hit_divisions: Reference-count stripe indexing in clockcache_try_get_read and clockcache_unget still divides by cfg->cacheline_capacity. Those divisions predate the invalid-address branch and are unaffected. Do not report a division-free full get/unget operation.

register_frames.sync_main_and_mask_main: six callee-saved pushes, 0x38 frame; register renaming but same lifetime shape
register_frames.sync_original_and_mask_original: six callee-saved pushes, 0x38 frame; masks preserve layout and blocking spill location
register_frames.async_main_and_mask_main: one callee-saved push, no explicit frame allocation
register_frames.async_original_and_mask_original: four callee-saved pushes, 8-byte frame; membership logic remains inlined so mask does not eliminate extra saved registers

analysis.mask_original_hot_code_difference: Same control flow after address validation. Removing xor edx,edx and div is balanced in code size/instruction count by mask creation and register movement; latency improvement is the reason to test this variant.
nonblocking_miss_comparison: Main performs alignment and lookup bounds validation, sees UNMAPPED, and directly returns STATUS_BUSY for blocking==FALSE.
The invalid-address branch must additionally establish allocation membership before deciding STATUS_BUSY versus STATUS_BAD_PARAM, even when the caller requests no disk I/O.
That added work includes virtual allocator configuration access, its alignment/bounds/extent-zero checks, and reference-count lookup. No such work runs on valid resident hits.

For blocking misses, both main and original already validate allocator membership once: main in acquire_entry_for_load, branch before invoking disk-load helper. The branch changes ordering and error propagation rather than adding a second successful validation.

A pure nonblocking miss benchmark therefore measures deliberately stronger semantics and should be distinguished from resident-hit regressions. No claim of avoidable overhead or required optimization follows without workload evidence.
analysis.validation: Existing binary disassembly and source review only; no benchmark or executable run.
